faq.a: Aayat is associated with the Arabic form آيات, whose core sense is signs, verses, evidences.

faq.q: What is the origin of Aayat?
faq.a: Aayat is associated with Arabic. Plural of آية (āya, 'sign, verse'). Widely used as a given name in South Asia.
Yes — the underlying form آيات is Arabic.
Aayat can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.

Aayat should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. آيات is the plural of آية and occurs in the Qur'an as a common noun ('signs, verses'); it is not a Qur'anic proper name

faq.q: What are the variants of Aayat?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Aayat, aayat, ayat. Script forms are آيات, آیات, आयत.

faq.q: Is Aayat a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
